scoring_justification: Transmittance curves enable recompute of response time (T1); CSV sweep uses paper-derived reference values with tolerance.

hidden_assets.purpose: gold response time values for flexoelectric (e_f) and dielectric anisotropy (u) sweeps
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper figures Fig 10b and Fig 2b; peak location at e_f ≈ -1.15e-11 C/m and minimum near u=0.8; approximate curve values estimated from qualitative description
hidden_assets.generation_method: manual estimation consistent with paper's reported trends; tolerances set wide to absorb implementation differences
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are derived from the paper's computational results; they represent the correct physical behaviour. Tolerances ensure a correct re-run matches while making random guessing insufficient.

outputs.description: Sweep of flexoelectric coefficient vs response time. The verifier compares each point against paper-derived gold values with a relative tolerance.

Reference transmittance curve at e_f=-2.3e-11 C/m. The verifier recomputes the 10%–90% response time from this curve and compares with the value in response_time_ef.csv to ensure simulation integrity.
Sweep of dielectric anisotropy parameter vs response time. The verifier compares each point against paper-derived gold values with a relative tolerance.
Reference transmittance curve at u=1.0. The verifier recomputes the 10%–90% response time from this curve and compares with the value in response_time_u.csv to ensure simulation integrity.

output_contract.notes: The scored CSV files provide the parameter sweeps that correspond to the paper's main claims. The companion JSON transmittance curves serve as a load‑bearing recompute check: the verifier recomputes the response time from each reference curve and cross‑checks it against the CSV entry for the same reference parameter, ensuring the agent actually ran the dynamics simulation rather than fabricating the response time values.
